subject: The Designed Manufactured Installed promise
hook: No wall in a British house is truly straight
ig:
No wall in a British house is truly straight.

Plaster bows, corners lean and older homes around Stoke-on-Trent often have walls that wander noticeably from floor to ceiling. Furniture, on the other hand, is made straight and square.

The bit that reconciles the two is the filler: a strip of matching board at the end of a run, scribed on site. Our fitter traces the wall's exact profile onto the filler and cuts it to follow every bump, so the furniture meets the wall without a tapering gap.

This is why the 'installed' part of designed, manufactured, installed matters. The design allows room for fillers, the workshop makes them in the matching finish, and the fitter shapes them to your room.

Look at the end of your current wardrobe or kitchen run. Is there a gap? Tell us what you find.
fb:
Have a look at the end of your wardrobe or kitchen run. Is there a gap that gets wider towards the top?

That's because walls are rarely straight, especially in older houses, while furniture is built square. The fix is a scribed filler: a strip of matching board our fitters shape on site to follow the wall's exact profile, so the furniture meets the wall properly.

It's one of those details that only works when design, workshop and fitting team are all on the same page. More about our installation service here:
